newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close lower, following Wall St lead.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close lower, following Wall St lead.

text.p: Dutch shares finished lower on Wednesday, rebounding from Tuesday's record closing high after a near 80 point sell-off overnight on Wall Street.

Dealers said selling was moderate and some degree of profit taking here was to be expected in a market which has rallied consistently throughout the year. But opinion about the next move in the AEX index is beginning to split with some seeing a correction near-term and others seeing further gains.
The AEX closed 5.56 points down at 630.81, giving back over half of yesterday's 9.13 point gain but holding well above the 630.00 support level after a brief slip down to 629.66.
Dealers said the overnight drop on Wall Street, triggered as investors took profits after a month of spectacular gains, could make European players nervous of a more sustained sell off.

"We believe investors will now take a wait and see attitude. We feel that almost all the positive elements -- lower interest rates, high liquidity -- have done their work in the short term," said one dealer.

"Looking at Wall Street we've seen gains, but yesterday we saw the first firm setback (of 1.21 percent). We think a setback of five percent is possible if it becomes more and more clear that economic strength in the U.S. will go on," he said.

A lower opening on Wednesday in New York and a push downwards in the bond market after a weak start gave investors little reason to buy, and profit taking picked up speed a little during the afternoon, dealers said.
Some dealers characterised today's decline as a welcome consolidation based on light selling interest.

One said today's declines had to be seen in context of a bullish market whose fundamentals of low interest rates, underlying bond market strength, strong dollar and stable corporate earnings remained firmly in place. "We just don't see a convincing reason for the market to go down," he said.
